description: Priority-driven Sanity schema expansion plan to improve SEO, media handling, profile consistency, editorial control, and content maintainability for the portfolio.

planSummary.goal: Expand the Sanity content model so the portfolio becomes easier to manage, safer to maintain, and more flexible for future editorial updates.
approach: Start with site-wide SEO and media settings so the most reused concerns are centralized first.
Formalize the profile singleton as the canonical identity/contact source.
Enrich asset metadata and the most important showcase content types (projects and experience).
Improve blog metadata, navigation/footer links, and testimonial handling.
Expand siteSettings and add content status / preview helpers once core content structure is stable.
nonGoals: Rewriting the portfolio UI beyond what is needed to consume the new schema fields.
Removing existing content sources before the new schema paths are validated.
Adding unrelated CMS collections that do not support the portfolio directly.

priorityPlan.title: Add seoSettings singleton
priorityPlan.why: Controls metadata and search behavior centrally.
deliverables: Runtime wiring plan for site metadata
acceptanceCriteria: Site title, description, canonical URL, and social preview settings are editable in Sanity.
Noindex / nofollow behavior can be controlled without code changes.

priorityPlan.title: Add mediaSettings singleton
priorityPlan.why: Standardizes media defaults and improves accessibility consistency.
deliverables: Fallback image and alt guidance fields
Image quality and aspect preset fields
acceptanceCriteria: Asset metadata can be reused across sections without duplicating logic.

priorityPlan.title: Formalize profile singleton
priorityPlan.why: Creates one authoritative source for identity and contact details.
deliverables: Contact and social link canonical fields
acceptanceCriteria: Name, title, bio, avatar, and contact methods live in one profile record.
The runtime can consume the profile as a single source of truth.

priorityPlan.title: Enrich asset metadata
priorityPlan.why: Improves accessibility, editorial quality, and reuse of media.
deliverables: alt text, caption, credit, source, license fields
acceptanceCriteria: Media-bearing schemas can carry editorial metadata consistently.
The UI can surface richer image information where needed.

priorityPlan.title: Expand projects and experience
priorityPlan.why: These are the strongest portfolio showcase areas.
deliverables: Project sort order, status, and impact metrics
Experience achievements, tools, logo, gallery, and story fields
acceptanceCriteria: Projects and experience can tell a richer story without hardcoding in the app.
The schemas support featured content and editorial ordering.

priorityPlan.title: Improve blog metadata and link centralization
priorityPlan.why: Blog and global links benefit from better editorial control.
acceptanceCriteria: Blog posts can be published with better metadata.

priorityPlan.title: Replace placeholder recommendations
priorityPlan.why: Testimonials need to be editor-managed and credible.
acceptanceCriteria: Placeholder content can be replaced with real entries.
The model is simple enough for ongoing maintenance.

priorityPlan.title: Expand siteSettings and status fields
priorityPlan.why: Helps keep copy and editorial intent centralized.
deliverables: Section copy and CTA label fields
acceptanceCriteria: Global copy and content state can be adjusted in Sanity.
Content lifecycle is explicit in the schema.

priorityPlan.title: Add preview and revalidation helpers
priorityPlan.why: Supports safer editorial workflows after content structure is expanded.
acceptanceCriteria: Preview and refresh flows remain documented in the CMS.
Operational content is discoverable in Studio.

successMetrics.editorialControl: The most reused site-wide concerns live in Sanity, not hardcoded in the app.
successMetrics.mediaQuality: Assets have consistent metadata and fallback behavior.
successMetrics.contentFlexibility: Projects, experience, and blog content can evolve without code churn.
successMetrics.maintainability: Navigation, footer, and status handling are centralized and predictable.
successMetrics.workflow: Preview and revalidation notes stay documented alongside the schema.

agentContinuationPrompt: Read SANITY_SCHEMA_ENHANCEMENT_PLAN.md, SANITY_SCHEMA_ENHANCEMENT_PRD.json, progress.txt, studio/schemaTypes/*, src/lib/cms-content.server.ts, src/types/index.ts, and the affected components before writing code.
Work in very small slices and treat each slice as a self-contained deliverable.
After every completed slice, docs-only tweak, prompt update, or refinement, run the relevant validation, stage all changes, and create one conventional local commit before starting the next slice.
Commit every update, every change, and every docs-only refinement so the history stays granular, reviewable, and easy to bisect.
Do not bundle unrelated slices together; one slice equals one local commit.
Start with SCHEMA-001 and SCHEMA-002: seoSettings and mediaSettings.
Then implement profile singleton adoption and asset metadata enrichment.
Then expand projects and experience schemas.
Then add blog metadata, navigation/footer management, and testimonial improvements.
Then expand siteSettings, add status fields, and add preview/revalidation helpers.
Update runtime loaders and component consumers when schema changes require it.
Do not move on to later schema or runtime work until the current slice is implemented, validated, recorded, and committed.
Preserve existing content and fallback behavior unless a slice explicitly replaces it.
After each commit, immediately continue to the next eligible slice unless a genuine blocker requires user input.
